name: Robert Mercer

summary.text: Robert Mercer is a computer scientist and former co-chief executive of the hedge fund Renaissance Technologies, who stepped down from that role in 2017, and a major Republican donor. Press reports, citing The New York Times, say he invested $15 million in Cambridge Analytica, that the Mercer family invested in the firm in 2014 and brought on Steve Bannon as vice president, and that the firm was partly owned by Mercer and his family. In 2021 Renaissance executives including Mercer agreed to pay up to $7 billion to resolve an IRS dispute over the Medallion fund's tax treatment, a dispute that originated in a 2014 Senate subcommittee report.

facts.claim: Fox News, citing The New York Times, reported that Cambridge Analytica received a $15 million investment from Robert Mercer, a billionaire Republican donor; CNN reported that the Mercers invested in the firm in 2014 and brought on Steve Bannon as vice president, and that the firm was partly owned by Mercer and his family.

facts.claim: Mercer served as co-chief executive of Renaissance Technologies until stepping down in 2017 amid backlash over his political activism, Fox Business reported.
facts.quote: Bob Mercer, a prominent Trump backer, leaving hedge fund

facts.claim: In September 2021 Renaissance Technologies' current and former executives, including James Simons and Robert Mercer, agreed to personally pay as much as $7 billion in back taxes, interest and penalties to resolve a long-running IRS dispute over the Medallion fund's use of basket options to treat short-term gains as long-term returns. A bipartisan Senate panel had estimated in 2014 that Medallion investors underpaid taxes by some $6.8 billion.

openQuestions: The $15 million figure originates in New York Times reporting that could not be opened; the claim rests on Fox News and CNN accounts of it. A primary record of the Mercer family's shareholding in Cambridge Analytica LLC or SCL was not found.
The final terms of the 2021 Renaissance IRS settlement and Mercer's individual share were not found; the $7 billion is the reported ceiling.

A full FEC tally of Mercer's political giving was not compiled; only the 2017-2018 Remember Mississippi contributions were documented. Renaissance Technologies is not an entity on the site, so no connection was recorded for it.
The Jackson Free Press headline's phrase 'implicated in Russia probe' is the outlet's characterization and is not recorded as a fact here.
